statement: For a family A of subsets of L with support S=union A, the following are equivalent: every x∈S has a least member A(x) containing it; (α) each intersection A∩B is a union of members contained in A∩B and (β) every x∈S lies in some member minimal among those containing x; (γ) nonempty residuals A°=A minus union of proper submembers partition S, (δ) every member is a union of residuals, and (η) A° nonempty and A°⊆B imply A⊆B. This is pre-admissibility; admissibility additionally requires all residuals nonempty.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The quantifier x∈L in the printed first condition must be restricted to the support unless coverage L=S is assumed. β is the missing condition in IV scan27; this is an explicit later repair, not an independent new claim. “Minimal” is among members through x, not a globally minimal member.

his_statement: Si F est finie ... artinien ... Exemple idiot
statement: Condition β is automatic if the membership posets are well founded, in particular for a finite family; it may fail for an infinite descending chain with nonempty intersection. The attempted finite counterexample to independence of η is rejected on the page; the margin directs to VIII manuscript44–45 for a corrected infinite example.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Use VIII scans53–54 for the actual independence example. The cancelled finite example has no evidential force. For the failure of β use A_n=[0,1/n] (n≥1): intersections are members but 0 belongs to no minimal member.

statement: Admissible families of subsets of L are in bijection with pairs (S,R), where S⊆L and R is a preorder on S: take the distinct principal lower sets ↓x, with residuals the R-equivalence classes. Equivalently take a poset I and a surjection S→I, up to isomorphism of I. Equivalently take an Alexandrov topology on S, with lower sets closed. The empty family corresponds to S=∅. A pre-admissible family is obtained from its nonempty-residual core by adjoining redundant closed saturated subsets.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The preorder, not merely its equivalence relation, is needed. No finiteness is required for this representation. The margin about a “finite” core, if read literally, is unjustified and is listed for scan review.

his_statement: localement fermées ... convexes ... algèbre de Boole
statement: For an admissible family represented by S→I, saturated subsets are inverse images of subsets of I; closed saturated subsets correspond to lower sets, open saturated subsets to upper sets, and locally closed saturated subsets to order-convex subsets. If the family is finite, the Boolean algebra generated by its closed strata consists of all saturated subsets, with residuals as atoms.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The finiteness insertion is essential: an infinite family need not generate every union of its atoms under finite Boolean operations.

statement: A lower subfamily of an admissible family is admissible and keeps each retained stratum’s boundary and residual. Conversely an admissible subfamily is lower if its support is saturated and its induced partition is the restriction of the original partition.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Unlike mere set inclusion of families, lower-ideal inclusion preserves the residuals. This is the repaired subfigure notion of IV scan28.

statement: Two admissible families F,G are compatible iff their union is admissible and each is a lower subfamily; iff both are lower subfamilies of a common admissible family; iff F∩G is lower in both and |F∩G|=|F|∩|G|; iff their common support is closed in both induced Alexandrov spaces and their figures restricted there agree. Compatibility is detected on every pair of principal elementary subfigures.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Equality of the partitions on the overlap alone is insufficient: the lower orders must also agree. The family of closed strata and the family of their open residuals give the on-page warning.

statement: For compatible admissible figures, support inclusion is equivalent to subfigure inclusion; in particular equal supports imply equal figures. The ordered set of all admissible families has a least empty figure and all bounded joins, computed by union of families. Its completely join-irreducible figures are exactly those with a greatest closed stratum; each figure is the join of its principal elementary subfigures. In this concrete model these elementary figures are also completely join-prime for bounded joins.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The join-prime conclusion follows from literal union and is stronger than the ordinary irreducibility definition used in IV scan54.

statement: The manuscript claims all elementary admissible set figures form one comparison-connected poset, using a proposed external product F⊠G consisting of all nonempty unions A∪B (A∈F or ∅, B∈G or ∅) for disjoint supports. As transcribed this product is not admissible: with F={{a}} and G={{b}}, the member {a,b} has empty residual. For L={a,b} the five elementary figures have three comparison components, including the isolated one-stratum figure {L}.
computation: code/computations.py: set_figures_two_points and boxtimes_counterexample
present_status: Every hypothesis is checked by exhaustive enumeration. The printed residual/boundary formulas at14–15 are inconsistent; a product-of-sets instead of union-of-subsets reading would be a different construction and must be checked on the ink. The actual set-family claim is refuted, not merely unproved.

statement: In the full system of all admissible figures on a set L, disjointness is exactly disjointness of supports. Consequently biorthogonal virtual supports identify with subsets of L, and the saturated subcontrée associated to L′⊆L consists of figures whose support lies in L′.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Singleton-point figures supply every disjointness test. This special Boolean case does not imply the general virtual-support conjecture of IV scan69.

his_statement: spectre ... compactifié de Stone ... points isolés
statement: The Stone spectrum of P(L) is the Stone–Čech compactification of the discrete set L; its isolated points are exactly the principal ultrafilters indexed by L. For a compact zero-dimensional Hausdorff space X, finite clopen-stratum families recover clopen supports. Passing to arbitrary regular-open supports leads to the complete Boolean algebra RO(X), with complement int(X minus U), meet intersection for finite meets, and arbitrary joins int(cl(union U_i)).
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The regular-open replacement is a proposed model/completion, not a proof that every arbitrary union of clopen strata is already regular open. The first spectrum assertion is classical; notation on the page for regularization requires ink review.

statement: Any collection of admissible figures specified by hereditary conditions on closed strata or principal multistrata is stable under subfigures and existing bounded joins that preserve those conditions. A global local-finiteness restriction is generally stable only under finite joins, not arbitrary bounded joins. A figure is finite iff it is finitely generated by principal subfigures and every principal subfigure is finite.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Do not suppress the qualification on global restrictions. A poset realized by cells gives closed saturated subsets as lower-cell unions under the stated frontier/topology assumptions; this does not prove arbitrary CW complexes are regular.

statement: For admissible F,G, F refines G iff |F|⊆|G| and the identity inclusion is monotone for their preorders (continuous for Alexandrov topologies). Equivalent formulations: each residual of F lies in one residual of G and the induced map on stratum posets is monotone; or every F-stratum has a least containing G-stratum and every intersection with a G-stratum is F-closed. This relation is an order.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Antisymmetry follows because equal supports and mutual preorder inclusion give the same principal-lower-set family; a bijection of quotient index sets alone would not suffice.

statement: A refinement is a subdivision iff supports are equal, iff it is maximal among refinements under subfigure inclusion. If the support omits a point of G, adjoining the singleton figure at that point gives a strict larger refinement. Compatible joins of refinements of G still refine G; bounded versions extend to arbitrary joins.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Maximality here is in the subfigure order, not in refinement. Every old stratum is a union of new strata, with the monotone least-target condition retained.

statement: A refinement is represented by a commutative square of support inclusion and surjections to posets, with monotone least-target map. Inverse images of saturated, closed, open and locally closed sets retain those properties. The index map can be bijective without being an order isomorphism, so preserving the partition alone does not identify figures.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: A discrete two-point order mapping identically to a two-element chain gives the elementary example of a monotone bijection that is not an order isomorphism.

statement: F refines G iff F is a subfigure of some subdivision of G. Complete F to |G| by adding singleton strata for all x∈|G| minus |F|, with no extra relations between the new points and F. This is a figure refining G and containing F as a lower subfamily.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Two printed expressions reverse the required difference or substitute G for F in the equal-support case; these are scan-reading alarms, not silently corrected transcription.

statement: The author asks whether subfigure inclusion can be recovered intrinsically from refinement and subdivision alone. He proves in the set model that a proper subfigure has different support, and that a simultaneous subfigure and subdivision must be equal.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The order-recovery question is distinct from those necessary conditions. No general recovery theorem is inferred merely from preorder representation.

statement: For figures F,G represented by S→I and T→J, their refinement infimum has support S∩T and preorder the intersection of the two restricted preorders. Its index poset is the image of S∩T in I×J, with induced product order. Its closed strata are A_i∩B_j for the pairs with A_i°∩B_j° nonempty. This extends to arbitrary families. For compatible figures it equals ordinary family intersection.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: For arbitrary families the topology is the initial Alexandrov topology, not necessarily the ordinary initial topology. Empty-index infimum is the indiscrete figure on L (empty if L is empty).

statement: Intersection with G preserves refinement, subdivision, and subfigure inclusion. If F′≤F, then F′.G consists exactly of the strata of F.G contained in |F′|. For a subdivision H of F and a subfigure G≤F, H.G is the unique subfigure of H subdividing G. Thus C6 holds for all admissible set figures.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The margin correctly flags uniqueness as an additional step; it follows from the equality of supports and uniqueness of the closed restricted preorder. This verification is specific to the set/preorder model.

statement: If G≤F and G′ subdivides G, the family F′=G′∪(F minus G) is admissible, subdivides F, and induces G′ on G. The quotient-poset construction replaces the lower ideal J⊆I by J′→J, keeps I minus J, and sets j′≤u iff its image is ≤u in I. This F′ is the least finer Alexandrov topology extending the prescribed topology on |G|.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: Unlike the earlier abstract closed/augmented-stratum replacement rejected in IV scan48, this construction is valid for actual subsets. The leastness is established by the later topology argument scans40–45, not by the false common-stratum lemma.

statement: The claimed equivalence between (b) bijective least-target map on strata outside the prescribed subfigure, (c) unchanged outside open strata, and (d) retention of all outside closed strata is false as stated: b⇔c holds, but d need not imply them. Let S={a,b}, F={S}, G=G′=∅, F′={{a},S}. It is an admissible subdivision retaining the closed stratum S, but its residual is {b} rather than S and its target map has two elements over the one old stratum.
computation: code/computations.py: common_closed_stratum_counterexample
present_status: This is a separate gap from the author’s explicit later retraction of (b,c,d)⇒leastness. The common-closed-stratum lemma used at scan33 is not proved later in these folders and the two-point example refutes it.

statement: For a poset I, lower ideal J⊆I and monotone surjection h:J′→J, form K=J′ disjoint-union (I minus J), retaining the two internal orders and j′≤u iff h(j′)≤u in I. Then K is a poset, J′ is lower, and K→I is monotone and restricts to an isomorphism off J′. It is terminal among such squares with prescribed J′ and prescribed complement identification.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The terminal statement requires the displayed category and its morphisms to preserve both prescribed parts. It does not imply that every square bijective off J′ is the same order; mixed relations can be removed. The page’s hoped-for inference to the false characterization is rejected later.

his_statement: topologie finale ... toute réunion de fermés ... initiale
statement: Final topologies for maps from Alexandrov spaces are Alexandrov. Compatible figures glue along a common closed subspace with equal induced topologies; their join is the resulting final topology. Subfigures correspond exactly to closed induced subspaces; refinements are continuous support inclusions and subdivisions are finer Alexandrov topologies on a fixed support. Initial Alexandrov structures exist for arbitrary families and have the intersection of the pulled-back preorders.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The ordinary initial topology need not be Alexandrov for infinitely many maps; the author explicitly inserts “ultra” in the margin. This distinction is necessary for arbitrary meets.

statement: Let T be a closed subset of an arbitrary topological space (S,τ), and σ a topology on T finer than τ|T. There exists a least topology τ* finer than τ inducing σ. Its closed sets are exactly A∪B with A τ-closed in S and B σ-closed in T. Equivalently X∩U is τ|U-closed, X∩T is σ-closed, and clτ(X∩U)∩T⊆X∩T, where U=S minus T. The unique canonical representation is X=clτ(X∩U)∪(X∩T). If τ and σ are Alexandrov, so is τ*.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The later general proof repairs the defective distributive expansion at scan40. Closedness of T is used essentially when σ-closed B⊆T must be closed in every extending topology.

statement: For the least extension τ*, the closure formula is clτ*(X)=clτ(X∩U)∪clσ(X∩T). In particular every subset of U has the same closure in τ and τ*. In the Alexandrov case the preorder restricts to σ on T and to τ on U, retains all τ-relations x≤y with y∈U, and has no relation x∈U≤y∈T.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The scan49 final formula changes the proved union to intersection, which is false even on a singleton and is a high-weight reading alarm. The closure formula is valid without any separation axiom.

his_statement: topologie ... finale pour ... S et T
statement: The original topology τ is the final topology for the identity (S,τ*)→S and the inclusion (T,τ|T)→S. Equivalently X⊆S is τ-closed iff X is τ*-closed and X∩T is τ|T-closed. This holds without the Alexandrov or saturation restrictions.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The printed corollary says A a subset of T, which makes the test tautological; the proof and final-topology formulation require an arbitrary subset of S. Record as a reading alarm.

his_statement: Mais c’est faux !! ... C’est ultra faux
statement: The author retracts the claim that the least extension is characterized by being finer than τ, inducing σ on T, agreeing with τ on U, and recovering τ as the final topology of the extended S and old T. Its counterexample has S={u,a,b}, T={u,a}; τ identifies u,a and places both below b; σ is discrete; the least extension has u<b and a<b, while another allowed extension keeps only a<b. Both satisfy the four weak tests, but cl{b} differs.
computation: code/computations.py: author_three_point_extension
present_status: The final diagram appears to draw an extra arrow from u to b while the text says the closure is {a,b}; the stated closure determines the counterexample, but the drawing must be checked on scans. This is the author’s refutation, independently certified.

his_statement: condition ... pour A⊂U ... adhérence ... la même
statement: Within the topologies finer than τ and inducing σ on the closed T, the least extension is characterized by preservation of τ-closures of all subsets of U=S minus T. The closure formula of C-SA21-5-024 then determines it uniquely.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The surviving correction uses all subsets of U, not only preservation of the topology induced on U. In an Alexandrov space it suffices to test singleton subsets of U, since closure commutes with arbitrary unions.

statement: For the canonical replacement K→I of a closed subposet J by J′, if J′→J is a surjective quotient map of Alexandrov spaces, then K→I is a quotient map. The same holds for the quotient maps of the corresponding preorders.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: This follows from C-SA21-5-025 and the stipulated topology on the prescribed lower part. The first phrase reverses J and J′ in “topologie ... quotient” while the displayed map fixes the direction.

statement: For the canonical poset replacement map K→I, connectedness or weak contractibility of all point fibers is inherited from J′→J, because outside J the fibers are singletons. If each inverse image of a principal lower ideal of J is weakly contractible, the same holds for every principal lower ideal of I: outside J it has a greatest lift. The page further asserts preservation of universal weak homotopy equivalence under a “homotopiquement propre with weakly contractible fibers” package.
computation: No numerical computation; the set/order argument is described in CHECK_EVENTS.
present_status: The principal-ideal argument is explicit and can be compared exactly with Quillen’s Theorem A for posets. The universal statement needs a fixed definition of homotopically proper and the relevant category of base changes; it is not identified merely with ordinary Theorem A. The manuscript’s ≤ versus < and an I′ minus U′ occurrence are reading alarms.
